source_caption:
🎬 Brewster’s Millions (1985)

Brewster’s Millions follows Montgomery Brewster, a struggling minor-league baseball player whose life takes an extraordinary turn when he discovers that he could inherit a massive fortune from a wealthy relative. However, there’s one unusual condition: to receive the full $300 million inheritance, Brewster must spend $30 million in just 30 days while following a strict set of rules. He cannot simply give the money away, destroy valuable possessions, or reveal the real reason behind his outrageous spending. What initially seems like an easy opportunity quickly becomes a hilarious nightmare as Brewster purchases expensive items, hires countless employees, and makes increasingly ridiculous financial decisions. Alongside his loyal friend Spike Nolan, he encounters suspicious businessmen, unexpected complications, and people who question his sudden extravagant lifestyle. As the deadline approaches, Brewster discovers that spending money can sometimes be just as difficult as earning it. Combining clever humor, outrageous situations, and memorable performances, the film explores wealth, greed, friendship, honesty, and the true meaning of happiness.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Satire

⭐ IMDb: 6.5/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 42m • PG

🎥 Director: Walter Hill

🏆 Recognition: Starring Richard Pryor, John Candy, Lonette McKee, and Stephen Collins, the film became a memorable 1980s comedy thanks to Pryor’s energetic performance and entertaining chemistry with Candy. Based on George Barr McCutcheon’s 1902 novel, the story has received several film adaptations, with the 1985 version remaining one of its most recognizable interpretations.

source_details.synopsis: Brewster's Millions is a 1985 American comedy film directed by Walter Hill. The film stars Richard Pryor, John Candy, Lonette McKee, Stephen Collins, and Hume Cronyn. The screenplay by Herschel Weingrod and Timothy Harris was based on the 1902 novel of the same name by George Barr McCutcheon. It is the seventh film based on the story, and focusing on a Minor League Baseball pitcher who accepts a challenge to spend $30 million in 30 days in order to inherit $300 million from his great-uncle. The film was met with negative reviews. A sequel titled Brewster's Millions: Christmas was released on December 5, 2024.
